My family has worked this land for three generations. I am 70 years old and I have been farming since I was a boy. I know this land. I know Quzhou. The soil here is flat, the winters are cold and dry, the rains come in summer. I do not read books or go to meetings. I watch the sky and I remember what my father told me.

There is only one way I farm: wheat in the winter, corn in the summer. The same land, the same rotation, every year of my life. I plant wheat in October when the air turns cold, and I harvest it in June. The day after the combine leaves, I plant corn. I harvest the corn in late September before the cold returns. This is the rhythm. I do not change the rhythm.

I will farm 6 mu. My son helps during the busy periods — planting and harvest — but I manage the rest. I hire the village tractor man for tillage and the combine for harvest. My knees do not allow me to do this with animals anymore.

For wheat, I use the improved seed from the cooperative in town. Everyone in the village buys it there. I apply compound fertilizer before plowing and add urea at the jointing stage. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to settle the soil, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in early spring and spray again for aphids in May. I have done this my whole life.

For corn, I buy the hybrid seed — the same one I have used for years, the kind that yields well and everyone knows. After wheat harvest I disk the stubble lightly and plant directly. I apply urea at the big bell stage when the stalks are knee-high. Two irrigations if the summer rains are thin. One herbicide spray right after emergence, one spray for borers in August.

I do not experiment. A bad harvest at my age is something I cannot recover from.
